messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: HelioCorp (enterprise / VPC, dedicated pool) streaming websocket errors detected in us-west-2. 502 + WS resets above alert threshold. Pager: raj-sre, maya-platform. Incident ID INC-20260317-42

maya-platform: acked. taking it. looking at routing + runtime logs now.

raj-sre: quick summary from infra: spike of 502s and connection resets for tenant=heliocorp. new WS connections normal, but long-lived streams stall ~40-60s in. client-side reports 'stream stopped, no further tokens'.

olivia-support: customer reported multiple users seeing streams hang, filed support ticket — customer is on a public-facing app gateway with their own idle-timeout configs.

derek-ml: looping in eng-runtime for possible chunking/flush behavior. are we hitting buffer thresholds or larger frames that their appgw rejects?

maya-platform: runtime metrics: dedicated pool (heliocorp-usw2) shows increased per-token tail latency and KV-cache miss spike coincident with resets. throughput steady.

raj-sre: log snippet (relevant):
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] tenant=heliocorp stream_id=abc123 event=ws_frame_sent size=8192 status=200
[2026-03-17T14:02:56Z] tenant=heliocorp stream_id=abc123 event=ws_frame_send_error code=1006 err="connection reset by peer"
```

maya-platform: plausible causes: app gateway idle or proxy heuristics killing long frames; large single-frame writes; intermediate LB inadvertently resetting. mitigation options:
- ask customer to raise gateway idle-timeout (they control it)
- enable SSE fallback for this tenant (server-side routing)
- temporarily force non-stream responses (long-poll) for HelioCorp routes
- reduce runtime chunk size/flushing frequency to keep proxy alive (per-tenant config)

oncall-bot: raj-sre is primary; handoff scheduled to maya-platform in 30m if unresolved.

raj-sre: I'm going to apply two immediate mitigations: enable SSE fallback in routing for HelioCorp (canary 5%) and reduce runtime chunk size for that tenant to 2KB. Applying now.

deploy-bot: rollout started -> route-update/heliocorp: enable-sse-fallback (canary 5% -> 100%) [deploy/route-update/3912345678]

maya-platform: canary at 5% looks healthy so far, no 502s observed on canary sessions after 3 minutes.

olivia-support: messaged HelioCorp support: "We've enabled a streaming fallback and adjusted chunking on our side; please confirm if affected users resume." They replied: "Confirmed: one user in our QA environment recovered immediately."

derek-ml: monitoring: 502 rate dropped from ~52/min to ~6/min within 20 minutes after canary. streaming stalls count decreased similarly. Good sign.

maya-platform: creating incident ticket INC-20260317-42 with timeline and actions, assign to eng-runtime for RCA and follow-up. Recommend we ask customer to increase keepalive/idle-timeout to 120s and test larger frames behind their gateway.

raj-sre: handoff notes for next oncall: monitor HelioCorp tenant for 2h, watch 502 rate and WS-reset rate. escalate to SRE lead if >10% of sessions still failing.

maya-platform: thanks everyone :thumbsup: Closing active pager for now; I'll update the incident ticket with timeline, config diffs, and proposed next steps (postmortem, per-tenant chunking policy, and docs for customers running fronting app gateways).

olivia-support: adding customer-facing note and suggested config snippet to share with HelioCorp: 
```
# Recommended app gateway keepalive
idle_timeout = 120s
max_frame_size = 16KB
enable_chunked_flush = true
```

maya-platform: final: tagging eng-runtime + product-observability for follow-up. incident closed for paging, will keep ticket open for RCA.
